title: PR curation and sanity scratch
content:
Context / intent:
This is a personal scratchpad for triaging a small batch of inbound PRs that surfaced some instability and surprise latency regressions on the 2.1 branch. Goal is to quickly capture heuristics, tiny fixes, and follow-ups I can hand off or apply in <30m patches. Not a formal postmortem, just a working checklist and notes-to-self.

Quick summary of observed signals:
- CI flaky on unit-tests: majority failing in kv_cache tests (time-dependent).
- Production traces show a 7-15% P95 token latency bump after recent kernel selection change (PR 789).
- Small number of error logs tied to missing fallthrough when model-variant routing returns empty variant (edge case for quantized fallback).
- No clear memory increase; throughput stable.

Primary hypotheses (ranked):
1) Kernel selector now prefers a slightly different matmul path for short sequences; micro-op change increases overhead for the typical 32-token chat workload.
2) New async batching path has a scheduling jitter when batch size < 4, causing higher P95 tail.
3) Race in kv_cache invalidation triggered by rare request ordering in integration tests; causes test nondeterminism.

Immediate small fixes to try (<=30m each):
- Revert kernel selector heuristic in canary (quick revert commit) and run perf job for 2 hours. (PR-run: create PR with revert, label: perf-investigate)
- Add defensive guard to model-variant routing: if candidate list empty, log context including routing policy + request metadata (limit to 1/10k). Quick unit + integration test.
- Stabilize kv_cache test by adding deterministic clock or mock clock in test harness (wrap with TEST_CLOCK).

Fast review checklist (what I actually scan when reviewing the above PRs):
- Does the change modify kernel selection or scheduling code paths? If yes: search for microbenchmarks and perf job IDs.
- Any new global mutable state or new statics? Flag for SRE review.
- Do tests use real time.Sleep or non-deterministic timers? Prefer test clocks/mocks.
- Are feature flags or configs behind a rollout gate (canary) to toggle behavior? If not, request gating.
- Are observability hooks (traces/tags/counters) added where behavior changes? If not, request lightweight metrics.
- Does the PR touch batching logic? Check batch size sampling function and corner path when size==1.

Refactor ideas / medium follow-ups (30m-3d):
- Break kernel selection into deterministic policy interface + pluggable strategies so we can A/B kernel selection with runtime flag.
- Introduce a lightweight sampling profiler in canary that attaches to the short sequences path (sampling at 50ms) to capture scheduling jitter.
- Move kv_cache tests into an isolated hermetic docker-run to remove host timing variability.
- Add a small chaos test that randomizes ordering of async batch completions to catch race-like behaviors.

Owner and handoff notes:
- If I (Vivienne) am OOO, hand to Arjun for perf runs; give Maya the test harness patch to stabilize kv tests.
- Tag SRE for rollout gating if kernel revert is needed.

Follow-ups / tickets to open (tentative titles):
- ENGINF-XXXX: perf investigation: kernel-selector short-seq latency (assign Arjun)
- ENGINF-XXXX: stabilize kv_cache tests with deterministic clock (assign Maya)
- ENGINF-XXXX: add defensive empty-variant logging + metric (assign Vivienne)
- ENGINF-XXXX: batch-scheduling jitter sampler (spike, 2d)

Quick notes for PR description templates (copy into PRs I'm about to open):
- Revert rationale: brief perf delta + link to perf-job and traces.
- Tests: list unit/integration + explain any timing mocks.
- Rollout: recommend canary 1% traffic for 2 hours before wider rollout; monitoring hooks: P50/P95 token latency, fallback count, error rate.

Local commands I used / will use:
- ./tools/run_perf_job --branch=canary-revert --duration=2h --targets=shortseq
- ./tools/trace_dump --since=2025-11-06T00:00Z --filter="route:chat-32-token" > traces-789.log
- pytest tests/kv_cache_test.py::test_concurrent_invalidation -k deterministic -s

Loose thoughts / notes to self (untidy):
- If the revert reduces P95 by ~10% but increases P50 marginally, consider hybrid strategy: keep fast path for hot models only.
- Watch out for metric cardinality when adding new tags on routing log. Keep tag set small.
- Future: expose kernel selection summary in the model dashboard (console) so product can see variants impact.

Unresolved questions to ask on PR threads:
- Why did prior perf job not catch this? (sampling window, workload mismatch?)
- Which customers saw the regression, and do we have a reproducible trace linked to a customer request?

Status: draft scratchpad. Will convert to formal postmortem if revert/experiment shows clear causality.

TODO (ordered):
- [ ] open revert PR + tag perf job (Vivienne)
- [ ] post quick status to #infra-review with perf-job link (Vivienne)
- [ ] stabilize kv_cache tests and push CI fix (Maya)
- [ ] create tickets for follow-ups and map owners (Vivienne -> Arjun/Maya)
- [ ] schedule 30m sync with SRE if revert happens (coordinated rollout)

End of scratch.
